jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Process & Business Readiness *** Directeur(ice), Processus d'entreprise et préparation opérationnelle
jobs.description:
At IPEX, the leader in thermoplastic piping systems, we are redefining the future of water management and clean energy. As part of the Aliaxis family, we combine global strength with local expertise to tackle the world's toughest challenges. Guided by our values – We Care, We Dare, We Deliver – we challenge the status quo to make a meaningful impact. If you're an innovative collaborator ready to make a difference, come join us in shaping a better tomorrow!

Job Summary

The Director, Enterprise Process & Business Readiness is accountable for leading the business transformation activities required to successfully deploy SAP across the enterprise’s manufacturing and distribution network.

Reporting to the VP, ERP Business Transformation, this role serves as the senior business counterpart to the Director of ERP Delivery and is responsible for ensuring the organization is operationally prepared for the ERP deployment through process standardization, stakeholder alignment, organizational readiness, and deployment governance.

The role partners closely with the Director, ERP Change & Training, Director, Data Governance & Management, Business Process Owners, Functional Leaders, Site Leadership Teams, and IT to drive adoption of standardized SAP-enabled business processes across IPEX’s manufacturing plants and distribution centres.

The Director leads the enterprise-wide efforts to establish consistent operating practices, collaborate in the transformation of operational master data, mobilize business resources, and implement objective readiness measures that ensure successful deployment and business continuity during cutover and go-live.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Process Transformation

Lead enterprise process transformation by establishing the future-state business process model, leveraging SAP standard capabilities, leading practices and simplification opportunities
Dotted line partner with the Business Process Owners (BPOs) to document, sustain, and deploy future-state processes
Establish governance mechanisms to ensure adherence to standardized processes and minimize local customization
Drive alignment between enterprise process standards and site-level operational requirements
Resolve conflicts between local business practices and enterprise process design
Facilitate process harmonization workshops with functional and operational leadership teams
Ensure process design decisions support scalability, compliance, operational efficiency and SAP standard functionality
Own business governance, quality, and stewardship of operational master data across assigned process domains.
Approve and prioritize master data changes, ensuring compliance with data standards, controls, and business requirements.
Partner with Data Governance, Data Stewards, and IT teams to define, maintain, and continuously improve master data processes and controls.

Business Readiness

Develop and execute the enterprise business readiness strategy for ERP deployment
Identify points of failure, risks, business contingency plans, and the metrics that trigger identified contingencies
Develop key tactics to alter timing of typical business rhythms by advancing or deferring core activities or operations
Plan daily operations to compensate for reduced staffing during training period
Develop and deploy operational targets (KPIs), monitoring methods, and reporting cadence
Collaborate on planning staffing levels to compensate for loss of efficiency during Hypercare
Ensure employees understand any role or responsibility changes
Determine key user and backfill needs; outline coverage and working schedule
Support external business partners on key actions and dates to align changes within their operations
Identify operational leader roles for Cutover and Hypercare coverage
Identify leaders responsible for cascading information
Create opportunities to share transparent, timely updates
Identify potential roadblocks to successful transfer to Business ownership
Plan supervisors’ daily activities post-Go Live to support new ways of working and identify issues early
Drive stakeholder engagement across manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, customer service, finance and commercial functions
Build commitment and ownership among operational leaders for adopting for adopting new ways of working
Lead readiness reviews with executive stakeholders and deployment governance teams
Partner with Operational Change Management & Training to ensure training, process adoption, organizational readiness, and business ownership are achieved before deployment

Job Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, Business; MBA considered beneficial
10-15 years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, operations, ERP transformation, or operational excellence
Proven experience leading large-scale, multi-year ERP deployments, preferably SAP
Experience deploying standardized business processes across multiple manufacturing locations
Experience establishing operational master data governance and quality programs
Experience influencing senior leaders across operational and functional organizations
Demonstrated success leading enterprise-wide transformation initiatives

IPEX is committed to providing accommodations for people with disabilities throughout the recruitment process and, upon request, will work with qualified job applicants to provide suitable accommodation in a manner that takes into account the applicant’s accessibility needs due to disability. Accommodation requests are available to candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process for IPEX jobs. To request an accommodation, please contact HR at HR@ipexna.com

jobs.title: Site Finance Leader
jobs.description:
Eaton’s Electrical sector is currently seeking a Site Finance Leader to join our CPDI team. This hybrid position is based at our Toronto, ON facility and offers benefits from day one.

The expected annual salary range for this role is $93000 - $117000 a year.

Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.

What You’ll Do

The Site Finance Manager provides direct financial leadership for the Critical Power and Digital Infrastructure business unit, serving as a strategic business partner and change agent to drive continuous improvement and achieve overall business objectives.

This role partners closely with Operations, Sales, Service, and Supply Chain teams to provide financial guidance and actionable insights, drive accountability, and help ensure business strategies and decisions deliver the expected financial and operational results.

Key Responsibilities Include

Analyze financial data and operational performance metrics to identify trends, opportunities, and areas for improvement. Partner with operational leaders to establish key performance indicators (KPIs) and drive accountability for results.
Provide financial insights and analysis to support business decision-making, including capital investment opportunities and resource prioritization.
Drive productivity and profitability through operational excellence, effective supply chain management, and disciplined budget management across the region.
Build organizational capability across both sites by supporting talent development, organizational design, and succession planning.
Partner with Operations to develop action plans, strategies, and initiatives based on financial insights. Monitor execution and measure results through appropriate KPIs.
Develop financial models and scenario analyses to assess potential impacts on operational and financial performance.
Identify financial and operational risks and recommend appropriate mitigation strategies.
Monitor and manage operational costs to improve efficiency and reduce costs while maintaining quality and business performance.
Lead inventory control actions and initiatives to improve operational profitability and optimize cash flow.
Coordinate profit planning and forecasting activities, including analysis of key operational metrics and manufacturing costs.
Lead the planning and deployment of capital investments to support short-, medium-, and long-term business needs. Ensure capital is appropriately prioritized and allocated based on business requirements and cash flow.
Guide sites through Finance Transformation initiatives, including leading change management efforts and implementing best practices that strengthen financial and operational performance.

Qualifications

Basic Required Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field.
Minimum of 5 years of progressive accounting, finance, or controllership experience.
Minimum of 3 years of experience in an operations or manufacturing environment.
Must be legally authorized to work in Canada without company sponsorship now or in the future.
No relocation is offered.

Preferred Qualifications

CPA designation or actively pursuing a CPA designation. CFA or other relevant professional financial designation is considered an asset.
Strong knowledge of Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) requirements.
Demonstrated experience with financial and data analytics, including translating complex financial information into actionable business insights.
Knowledge of Canadian federal and provincial tax laws and regulations.
Understanding of foreign currency transactions, translation, and financial reporting requirements.
Experience with Oracle Financials or similar ERP systems, including financial system integration.
Strong knowledge of internal controls, financial governance, and risk management.
Experience supporting financial planning, forecasting, budgeting, and manufacturing cost analysis.
Experience partnering with Operations, Supply Chain, Sales, or other cross-functional teams in a manufacturing environment.

What Makes You Successful

You’re a collaborative and proactive finance professional who enjoys turning data into meaningful business insights. You communicate financial concepts in a clear and practical way, build trusted relationships across teams, and are comfortable working in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. You bring strong analytical and Excel skills, manage priorities effectively, and enjoy staying connected to the business by partnering closely with manufacturing teams, including spending time on the shop floor and occasionally visiting other sites.

All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

At Eaton we leverage artificial intelligence to recommend jobs to you that match the skills and experience required for the open role. Our Talent Acquisition teams also uses AI to identify applicants whose skills are a match for the job. Hiring decisions are made by Eaton leaders through a structured interview process and not AI.

Eaton has in place accessibility policies for accommodating employees with disabilities. If you are selected for an interview and require accommodations, please let the recruiter or hiring manager know so that we can work to make reasonable adjustments that best suit your needs. Accessibility information may be found at: http://www.eatoncanada.ca/EatonCA/OurCompany/Accessibility/index.htm

We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for job applicants and employees. Our recruitment processes use balanced selection criteria and avoid unlawful discrimination against applicants on the basis of their age, colour, disability, marital status, national origin, gender, gender identity, genetic information, race or racial origin, religion, sexual orientation or any other status protected or required by law.

We know that good benefit programs are important to employees and their families. Eaton provides various Health and Welfare benefits as well as Retirement benefits, and several programs that provide for paid and unpaid time away from work. Click Benefits at Eaton Canada / Avantages sociaux chez Eaton Canada for more detail. jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Company Description
Mazda Gaspé is an automotive dealership focused on delivering reliable vehicles and responsive customer service. The organization values transparency, operational efficiency, and sustainable business practices across sales, service, and financing activities. Team members collaborate to create a positive experience for clients while maintaining strong financial and operational performance. The company supports modern work practices, including remote collaboration, and encourages continuous improvement in all areas of the business.
Role Description
The Chief Financial Officer (CFO) at Mazda Gaspé is a part-time, remote role responsible for overseeing the company’s overall financial strategy and performance. The CFO will manage budgeting and forecasting, monitor cash flow, and provide financial guidance to leadership to support decision-making and long-term growth. Daily tasks include reviewing financial statements, ensuring accurate financial reporting, and maintaining compliance with relevant accounting standards and regulations. The CFO will collaborate with internal teams and external partners to optimize financial processes, analyze risks and opportunities, and implement controls that support sustainable profitability. This role also involves preparing regular financial updates for management, advising on investments and capital allocation, and supporting strategic initiatives.
Qualifications

Strong foundation in Finance, with demonstrated experience in corporate or dealership financial management.
MUST BE LOCATED IN CANADA
Proficiency in Financial Planning and budgeting, including forecasting and cash flow management.
Ability to prepare, interpret, and review Financial Statements, ensuring accuracy and compliance.
Experience in Financial Reporting, including management reports and regulatory filings.
Advanced Analytical Skills, with the ability to assess financial performance and identify trends and risks.
Comfort with remote work tools, strong communication skills, and the ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams.
Experience in the automotive or retail sector is an asset.
Relevant academic background in finance, accounting, or business; professional designations (e.g., CPA, CFA) are an advantage.

jobs.title: Director, Strategy & Business Development
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Director, Strategy and Business Development, will be responsible for contributing to growing Seaspan Shipyards business by leading and implementing business strategies for new or growing markets. Interfacing with Seaspan’s senior leadership team, this role will lead and support a range of strategic plans and initiatives including broad new business strategies, transformational initiatives, strategic initiatives and complex captures.

Key to this role will be a strategic approach to understanding the breadth and complexity of our customer’s needs and developing strategies and solutions to meet those needs – both technical and non-technical. Working as part of the broader multi-disciplinary Seaspan team, this role will include direct leadership of strategic initiative teams collaborative interfaces to many other departments and teams within Seaspan. An important aspect of this role will be the development of business cases for our strategic initiatives including how they will generate long-term returns for Seaspan.

Note: This position qualifies for an optional hybrid work schedule after 90 days of onsite work and onboarding. Employee will be subject to the terms of the Flexible Work Policy Agreement.

What You'll Do

Drive future growth for the company through disciplined but creative strategy and business development.
Lead development and implementation of new business strategies targeting new or growing markets.
Lead implementation of strategic initiatives
Provide oversight, guidance and support to capture leads and their capture and proposal teams.
Lead activities to find and develop opportunities both with new potential customers and with existing customers.
Maintain key business development contacts with current and potential customers.
Build and lead capture teams and proposal teams as required for each approved opportunity.
Identify growth opportunities within international markets and work with the wider Seaspan organization to develop competitive export offerings.
Represent and advocate on behalf of Seaspan Shipyards at conferences, trades shows, and other industry events.
Interface with other departments and teams in the Seaspan organization to achieve objectives in a manner aligned with overall Seaspan priorities, strategies and processes.
Strong communication skills (verbal and written) with customers, partners, suppliers and within Seaspan.

What You'll Bring

10+ years of professional industry experience advancing complex new business development strategies and bid proposals in the shipbuilding industry or in a complex defence, aerospace or systems development, manufacturing or construction industry.
University degree in a relevant area preferred.
Proven track record of developing business strategies and then leading the implementation.
Experience leading and closing complex opportunities with contract values over $10M and ideally over $50M.
Broad understanding of technical, programmatic, financial and commercial aspects of complex deals.
Experience with forming and maintaining strategic industry partnerships and supplier arrangements as part of an overall strategy.
This job is both strategic and tactical, and requires substantial leadership in market/customer strategy and opportunity capture.
Multi-faceted leadership skills applicable to direct leadership roles and influential leadership roles.
Ability to work in a highly flexible and fluid environment and maintain calm and rational thinking and reasoning at all times.
Demonstrated ability to communicate with a variety of stakeholders and the ability to respond to stakeholder needs strategically and tactfully.
Exceptional interpersonal skills, superior oral and written capabilities, including the ability to build professional relationships with government and industry partners.
Skilled at advocacy, influence, and persuasion, with the able to convince others to act on information or recommendations based on compelling logic or common best interests.
Knowledge of complex government markets.
Strong knowledge and expertise with Microsoft Office (PowerPoint, Word, Project and Excel).
Self-starter with good organizational skills who can work both independently and as a member of a team.

Why you'll love working here

This is a full-time, permanent position. With multiple operations and long-term projects, Seaspan employees enjoy job stability as we look ahead to build ships for decades to come.
In addition to an annual bonus and pension plan matching, this role provides you a very competitive salary in line with the successful candidate’s experience.
We also provide a best-in-class health and wellness benefits package for this position, including such things as full health care (e.g. unlimited physiotherapy), dental, vision, life insurance, medical leave coverage, parental leave coverage, wellness/fitness reimbursement for memberships or registration fees, and an Employee Family Assistance Program (EFAP).
This position qualifies for an optional hybrid work schedule.
Parking is included and to assist those that are using transit, we operate a complimentary shuttle bus Monday through Friday with various pick up and drop off points around North Vancouver.

The estimated salary for this position is $180,000 - $220,000. In determining final salary, Seaspan considers many factors including the successful Candidate’s skills and experience as well as position location and internal equity. The final base salary offer will be at the Company’s sole discretion and presented as part of a competitive total compensation package.

About Us

Seaspan Shipyards is one of North America’s most modern shipyards and unique in its ability to provide a complete range of services including new construction, conversion, refit, repair and life-cycle maintenance work for Canada’s Coast Guard and Navy as well as commercial vessels including cruise-ships and deep-sea vessels. Seaspan Shipyards operations include Vancouver Shipyards, Vancouver Drydock and Victoria Shipyards.

To learn more, visit our website:
www.seaspan.com

This position may involve defense articles and/or technical data regulated by the U.S. International Traffic in Arms Regulations (“ITAR”) and the U.S. Arms Export Control Act. In compliance with ITAR, the successful candidate will be subject to a security clearance through the Canadian Controlled Goods Program as regulated by the Controlled Goods Regulations and Defense Production Act. The successful candidate will be required to maintain their security clearance throughout their employment in this position.

Seaspan is committed to Employment Equity, supports diversity in the workplace, and encourages applications from all qualified individuals including, women, members of visible minorities, Indigenous persons, and persons with disabilities. If you require any accommodations at any stage of the recruitment process, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruit@seaspan.com for confidential support. We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible environment.

jobs.title: Regional Director- Business Development, Private Enterprise
jobs.description:
Overview

At KPMG in Canada, our people bring their unique perspectives to Canada’s most important challenges. Here, you can build momentum that reaches beyond our business, develop skills for the future, and take ownership of your career with support at every stage. Join a firm where your career can make a difference.

KPMG is a leading professional services firm providing a comprehensive suite of solutions to our clients. We pride ourselves on delivering exceptional value, strategic insights, and tailored financial and operational services to businesses in our communities.

We are seeking a highly motivated and strategic Director of Business Development to lead our sales initiatives and drive growth across our local offices. In this role, you will be the face of our firm in your designated local geography, tasked with building robust relationships with private companies. You will leverage your strong financial acumen to understand clients' complex needs and articulate the full breadth of our services. Furthermore, you will act as a key liaison, working seamlessly with internal partners to deliver comprehensive solutions, while leading the overall sales function, running key meetings, and reporting on pipeline metrics.

What You Will Do

Relationship Building & Market Expansion

Proactively identify, target, and build strong relationships with key decision-makers and C-level executives at private companies within the local geography.
Act as a brand ambassador, networking extensively within the local business community to uncover new opportunities and expand market share.
Establish and execute territory-specific business development strategies to expand market presence and revenue opportunities.
Act as a trusted advisor and primary point of contact for prospective and existing business partners.
Attend networking events, industry conferences, community engagements, and stakeholder meetings to increase visibility and generate leads.

Sales Leadership & Pipeline Management

Lead the overarching sales function for the local offices you cover, establishing a culture of high performance and strategic growth.
Manage and coordinate critical sales meetings, presentations, and pitches to prospective clients.
Rigorously track and manage the sales pipeline, providing regular reporting on key initiatives, conversion rates, and revenue projections to senior leadership.
Maintain a robust pipeline of opportunities and ensure timely progression through the sales process.
Collaborate with leadership to establish sales goals, forecasts, and performance metrics.

Strategic Client Engagement & Financial Acumen

Utilize deep financial acumen to analyze client business models, understand their financial objectives, and identify areas where our firm can add quantifiable value.
Confidently discuss and cross-sell our full breadth of services, tailoring the value proposition to address specific financial and operational challenges.
Work closely with internal partners, operational teams, marketing, and leadership to align business development activities with organizational priorities.
Coordinate internal resources to support client engagement, proposal development, and implementation activities.
Facilitate communication between external partners and internal stakeholders to ensure successful project delivery and relationship management.
Contribute insights on market trends, customer needs, and competitive intelligence to support strategic planning.

Internal Collaboration & Partnership

Partner collaboratively with internal subject matter experts, practice leaders, and delivery teams to craft comprehensive, multi-service proposals.
Facilitate smooth handoffs from the sales process to the execution teams, ensuring client expectations are clearly communicated and met.
Drive internal alignment on go-to-market strategies and participate in strategic planning sessions.

What You Bring To The Role

Experience Minimum of 7 years of proven experience in B2B business development, sales leadership, or a related field, preferably within professional services, commercial real estate, or financial services.
Financial Acumen Strong understanding of corporate finance, financial statements, and business operations, with the ability to engage in high-level financial discussions with business owners and executives.
Relationship Management Demonstrated track record of building and maintaining a network of contacts within private companies and local business communities.
Communication Skills Exceptional presentation, negotiation, and written communication skills. Ability to translate complex service offerings into compelling value propositions.
Leadership Experience leading sales initiatives, managing pipelines (CRM proficiency), and reporting on key performance indicators.
Collaboration Highly collaborative team player with a history of successfully navigating matrixed organizations and working alongside internal partners to close deals.
Education Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, or a related field. (MBA, CPA or relevant advanced degree is a plus).

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

New business opportunities generated
Growth and quality of sales pipeline
Number of strategic relationships established and maintained
Revenue, partnership, or business development targets achieved
Conversion rates across sales stages
Client and partner engagement metrics
Timeliness and accuracy of reporting
Achievement of initiative and project milestones
Internal stakeholder satisfaction and collaboration effectiveness

Providing you with the support you need to be at your best

Our Values, The KPMG Way

Integrity
, we do what is right | Excellence
, we never stop learning and improving | Courage
, we think and act boldly | Together
, we respect each other and draw strength from our differences | For Better
, we do what matters

KPMG in Canada is a proud equal opportunities employer and we are committed to creating a respectful, inclusive and barrier-free workplace that allows all of our people to reach their full potential. A diverse workforce is key to our success and we believe in bringing your whole self to work. We welcome all qualified candidates to apply and hope you will choose KPMG in Canada as your employer of choice.

Adjustments and accommodations throughout the recruitment process

At KPMG, we are committed to fostering an inclusive recruitment process where all candidates can be themselves and excel. We aim to provide a positive experience and are prepared to offer adjustments or accommodations to help you perform at your best. Adjustments (informal requests), such as extra preparation time or the option for micro breaks during interviews, and accommodations (formal requests), such as accessible communication supports or technology aids, are tailored to individual needs and role requirements. You will have an opportunity to request an adjustment or accommodation at any point throughout the recruitment process. If you require support, please contact KPMG’s Employee Relations Service team by calling 1-888-466-4778.

AI Usage

We embrace the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance the candidate experience and streamline our recruitment processes. AI tools may help with organizing applications or surfacing relevant qualifications. However, no hiring decisions are made using AI. Every hiring decision is made by our hiring managers and recruitment professionals, who are equipped with training that empowers them to use these tools responsibly. AI technologies used in our recruitment process undergo detailed risk assessments, including security and privacy requirements, that align with KPMG’s Trusted AI framework.

We believe technology should empower human judgment, not replace it. It’s one of the many ways we’re delivering on our vision of being a technology-first, people-driven firm.
